speaker: Doctor
text: How would you describe the involuntary movements you are experiencing? Are they rhythmic and repetitive, or rather sudden and jerky? When did these movements first start in relation to your psychiatric diagnosis?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful. To narrow down the type of movement disorder, do you notice these movements occurring only when you are relaxed and sitting still, or do they persist even when you are actively engaged in a task?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your description of an inability to remain still, fidgeting, and leg crossing while on risperidone, I suspect you are experiencing Akathisia, a common extrapyramidal side effect. Before confirming this, do you feel any internal sense of agitation or urge to move your legs internally?

REQUEST TEST: Risperidone dosage and duration review.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Akathisia secondary to Risperidone therapy.
